narratives.narrative: Sense 101 reads the movement as 'seek the LORD', typed 102 as volition - an act of the will, not a passion undergone. Source 103 is present:false: the verse does not trace the seeking back to any prior interior cause; it stands as the self's own orientation. Seat 104 is 'none' - the operation is not lodged in an organ (no heart, no reins); it is a whole-person disposition, not a faculty. Bearer 105 is 'those who seek', target 107 is the seeking itself, and coupling 112 is 'seek-the-LORD': the operation 106 is the self and its kind sustaining a turn toward God and, on that ground, not being forsaken. Manner 108 is 'none', and intensity 109, specifier 110 and effect 111 are all present:false - the text does not colour how intensely or in what mode it is done, nor name a downstream effect beyond the not-forsaking already in the operation. Prohibition 113 present:false: nothing is forbidden here. Discovery 114 fixes it: v10, 'you have not forsaken those who SEEK you' - the interior orientation of seeking is the condition God honours, a directed reaching after him. Locus 116 is internal:ib-state and role 115 is characteristic: within the inner life this is a settled Godward set of the whole self, held up as the security of the one who knows God's name.
narratives.story: Here the psalm speaks of those who seek the Lord. It is something a person chooses and keeps doing, a steady turning of the whole self toward God rather than a feeling that sweeps over them. The verse does not say what first moved them to it, nor does it locate it in one part of a person; it is simply how they are set. Their reward is stated plainly: God has not forsaken those who seek him. Nothing is added about how hard or how fiercely they seek, and nothing is forbidden; the turning toward God, and the being held by him, is the whole of it.
narratives.variation_note: As the opening darash reading, this is seeking held up simply as the security of the faithful - those who seek God are not forsaken. It differs from Psa 10:4 (the proud who will not seek), Psa 14:2 (God searching for a seeker he scarcely finds), and Psa 34:10 (seeking answered with provision): here the finding is the bare covenant assurance that the seeker is never abandoned.

narratives.narrative: This is the dark counter-reading of the same item. Sense 101 is 'pride crowds God out' and type 102 shifts to cognition - where the God-seeker's turn was volitional, here the failure to seek is a settled state of mind. Source 103 present:false: the not-seeking is not derived from a named cause outside itself, yet the operation 106 supplies its interior ground - 'in the pride of his face the wicked will not seek God; there is no God is the whole content of his thoughts'. Seat 104 'none': again not organ-located; it is the cast of the whole self. Bearer 105 is 'the wicked', target 107 is practical-atheism, coupling 112 is 'no-room-for-God' - pride so fills the interior that God is absent from every calculation. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false - the descent is not intensified or given an outcome; the absence of seeking IS the condition. Prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: v4 names it as a mind so full of self that God does not enter its thinking. Locus 116 internal:ib-state, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is the interior organised around its own pride to the exclusion of God - seeking read in its negative, given the same analytic weight as its positive.
narratives.story: The same act appears here in reverse. The proud man does not seek God at all, and this is not a passing mood but the whole shape of his thinking: God simply has no place in it. His pride fills him so completely that, as he reckons things, there is no God to consider. Nothing outside him is blamed for this; it is who he is. No consequence is spelled out and nothing is forbidden - the point is the emptiness itself, a mind with no room left for God.
narratives.variation_note: Against the other H1875 seek readings, which are volitional turnings TOWARD God, this one is the operation in its absence: pride's cognition (type shifts from volition to cognition) that will not seek. The difference is the finding - the same characteristic read as descent rather than ascent, its bearer the wicked rather than the faithful.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'any who seek after God', type 102 volition. Source 103 present:false - the seeking is not attributed to an antecedent cause; it is the self's own reaching. Seat 104 'none': not organ-bound. Bearer 105 'the seeker', target 107 God-seeking, coupling 112 'seek-after-God'. Operation 106: the LORD looks down to see if any understand and seek after God - the rare interior that reaches for him. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false - the text does not grade or resolve it; the finding is simply the presence or absence of the seeking mind. Prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: v2 pairs understanding with seeking - the operation God searches the earth for is a mind that turns toward him; it is what marks a person as not-a-fool. Locus 116 internal:ib-state, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life, seeking here is the distinguishing interior God scans humanity to find, and (in this psalm's verdict) scarcely finds.
narratives.story: God looks down from heaven over all people to see whether anyone understands and seeks him. Seeking here is a turning of the mind toward God, the very thing that separates a wise person from a fool. It is not traced to any cause; it is simply what a person is or is not doing. The verse grades nothing and forbids nothing - it only asks whether the searching heart is there, and the psalm's sober answer is that it is rare.
narratives.variation_note: Distinct from the other seek readings by its vantage: God is the one searching for the seeker. Where Psa 9:10 rewards the seeker and Psa 10:4 shows the proud who will not seek, here the operation is held up as the scarce interior God hunts across all mankind - seeking as the mark of the non-fool.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'the seekers shall praise and live', and type 102 is affect - a notable shift: the seeking is read here through the register of feeling and its satisfaction rather than bare will. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none' - not organ-located. Bearer 105 'those who seek him', target 107 seeking, coupling 112 'seek-and-live'. Operation 106: the afflicted eat and are satisfied; those who seek God praise him and their hearts live forever - seeking rewarded with life. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false, yet the operation already carries the outcome (satisfaction, praise, unending life of the heart). Prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: v26, 'those who SEEK him shall PRAISE... may your HEARTS LIVE forever' - the seeking interior is promised satisfaction and unending life; the afflicted's hunger is met. Locus 116 internal:ib-state, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life seeking here is the hungry orientation that God fills, so that the seeking heart lives.
narratives.story: The afflicted will eat and be satisfied, and those who seek God will praise him - and the psalm cries, may your hearts live forever. Seeking here is felt as hunger answered: the reaching of a starved inner self toward God, met and filled. Its reward is not just relief but praise and a heart that goes on living. Nothing is graded or forbidden; the promise is simply that the one who seeks God is satisfied and made to live.
narratives.variation_note: Here the item is typed as affect, not volition - seeking read as the hunger of the afflicted that is satisfied, its reward life and praise. This differs from the God-searches-for-seekers reading (Psa 14:2) and the not-forsaken reading (Psa 9:10) by resolving into satisfaction and enduring life of the heart.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'the generation that seeks God's face', type 102 volition. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none' - not organ-bound. Bearer 105 'those who seek', target 107 God-seeking, coupling 112 'seek-his-face'. Operation 106: such is the generation of those who seek God, who seek the face of the God of Jacob - a whole company oriented to seeking him. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false - the passage does not intensify or resolve the act; it identifies a people by it. Prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: v6 defines a people by the direction of its desire - the seeking of God's face is what marks them. Locus 116 internal:ib-state, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life seeking here is corporate and identifying, the shared Godward set that constitutes 'the generation' of the pure-handed and clean-hearted.
narratives.story: Those who may climb God's holy hill are described simply as the generation that seeks him, that seeks the face of the God of Jacob. Seeking here is what a whole people is known by - a shared turning toward God that defines who they are. It is chosen, not felt upon them, and it is not lodged in any one faculty; it is the direction of their desire. The verse names no degree and forbids nothing; the mark of this company is just this, that they seek God's face.
narratives.variation_note: This reading makes the item corporate and identity-forming - a whole generation defined by seeking God's face. It differs from the individual not-forsaken (Psa 9:10) and satisfied-hunger (Psa 22:26) readings by locating the seeking as the badge of a people rather than a personal reward.

narratives.narrative: A different Hebrew item (baqash) enters. Sense 101 'one thing I ask - to gaze on his beauty', type 102 volition. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none' - not organ-located. Bearer 105 'the psalmist', target 107 consolidated-longing, coupling 112 'one-thing-I-ask'. Operation 106: the self reduces all its desire to one thing - to dwell in God's house and gaze on his beauty; longing consolidated onto a single object. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false - the intensity is carried not by a graded field but by the structure of the operation itself (many wants collapsing into one). Prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: v4, the gathering of all wants into one; the interior's many desires collapse into the desire to behold God. Locus 116 internal:ib-state, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this seeking is the funnelling of the whole appetitive self onto a single Godward aim.
narratives.story: The psalmist says there is one thing he asks and will seek after: to live in God's house and gaze on his beauty. Seeking here is desire narrowed to a single point - all his many wants pulled together into one, the longing to behold God. It is chosen, and it is the set of his whole self rather than any one part of him. The verse does not measure how strongly he wants it; the force is in the fact that everything else has given way to this one thing.
narratives.variation_note: Within baqash's many readings, this is the item as consolidated inward longing for God - desire funnelled to one object. It differs sharply from the enemy-hunting readings (e.g. Psa 54:3, 63:9) that share the same verb but aim at a life to destroy: here the pursuit is Godward and unifying, there it is murderous.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'those who seek the LORD lack no good', type 102 affect. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'those who seek', target 107 satisfied-seeking, coupling 112 'seek-no-good-lacking'. Operation 106: the young lions hunger, but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing - seeking that is satisfied. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false, though the operation carries provision as its outcome. Prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: v10 marks this off from v4's seeking-freed-from-fear - here the seeking is answered with provision; the interior that seeks God wants for nothing good. Locus 116 internal:ib-state, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is the seeking self met with sufficiency, contrasted against strong predators left wanting.
narratives.story: Even young lions go hungry, the psalm says, but those who seek the Lord lack no good thing. Seeking here is the reaching of the inner self toward God that is answered with full provision. It is not measured or graded; the plain claim is that the seeker of God is never left without good. The contrast is deliberate: the strongest hunters may starve, yet the one who seeks God is supplied.
narratives.variation_note: The base source itself flags the distinction: this seeking is answered with provision (lack no good thing), whereas the same item at Psa 34:4 ('sought') is answered by deliverance from fear. Same psalm, two fruits of seeking - supply here, freedom from dread there.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'seek peace and pursue it', type 102 volition. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'the hearer' (the one being taught), target 107 peace-pursuit, coupling 112 'seek-and-pursue-peace'. Operation 106: the self teaches - turn from evil, do good, seek peace and pursue it; an active chase after peace. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false. Prohibition 113 present:false - though the surrounding instruction includes negatives (keep tongue from evil), the seek-item itself carries no prohibition field. Discovery 114: v14 makes peace a quarry - the interior does not merely wish peace but hunts it. Locus 116 internal:ib-state, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is seeking turned toward an abstract good, peace, pursued as actively as prey.
narratives.story: The teacher's charge is to turn from evil, do good, and seek peace and pursue it. Seeking here is not aimed at God or an enemy but at peace itself, and it is no idle wish - peace is hunted, chased down like something worth catching. It is a chosen disposition of the whole person. The verse sets no measure and lays no ban on the seeking itself; it simply makes peace the thing the inner self goes after with intent.
narratives.variation_note: Uniquely among baqash readings, the target is peace (an abstract good), not God and not a victim. It shares the verb's active, hunting force with the enemy readings but bends it toward a good end - seeking as the pursuit of peace rather than of harm.

narratives.narrative: The perfect-tense item (darash, 'sought'). Sense 101 'I sought the LORD, freed from fears', type 102 affect. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'the psalmist', target 107 fear-dissolving-seeking, coupling 112 'sought-and-freed'. Operation 106: the self sought the LORD, who answered and delivered it from all its fears - seeking that dissolves dread. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false, yet the operation itself names the outcome: fear emptied out. Prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: v4, the turning-to-God that empties the interior of its fears. Locus 116 internal:ib-state, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is completed seeking, a past act whose fruit is a self cleared of fear - seeking as the movement that transforms the emotional interior.
narratives.story: The psalmist looks back: I sought the Lord, and he answered me and freed me from all my fears. Seeking here is a turning to God already done, and its effect is felt in the emotions - dread drained away. It was his own act, not lodged in any one part of him but the reach of his whole self. The verse does not say how hard he sought; it simply reports that seeking God emptied him of fear.
narratives.variation_note: As the item in completed past tense with a named emotional outcome (fear dissolved), this differs from the Psa 78:34 'sought' reading where seeking is compelled by judgment, and from the Psa 119:45 'sought precepts' reading aimed at God's word. Here the object is God himself and the fruit is a fearless interior.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'may all who seek you rejoice', type 102 affect. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'those who seek', target 107 joyful-seeking, coupling 112 'seekers-rejoice'. Operation 106: the self prays that all who seek God may rejoice and be glad, and those who love his salvation say 'Great is the LORD' - seeking that ends in joyful praise. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false, the joy being carried inside the operation. Prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: v16 widens the self's own rescue into a prayer that all seekers share its joy. Locus 116 internal:ib-state, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is seeking read as a shared, outward-turning gladness - the rescued self wishing its joy onto the whole company of seekers.
narratives.story: From his own deliverance the psalmist prays outward: may all who seek God rejoice and be glad in him, and may those who love his salvation always say, 'Great is the Lord.' Seeking here overflows into shared joy - the rescued man wants every seeker of God to feel the gladness he feels. It is a chosen orientation of the heart, not tied to any one faculty. Nothing limits or forbids it; the seeking simply ends in praise, and he wishes that praise on all.
narratives.variation_note: This baqash reading turns seeking outward and communal, resolving in joy for all seekers - unlike the consolidated private longing of Psa 27:4 or the peace-pursuit of Psa 34:14. It is the mirror image of the same verb's enemy readings: here all who seek God rejoice, there enemies who seek a life are shamed.

narratives.narrative: A rare item here - chalah, 'seek favour / entreat'. Sense 101 'seek favour / entreat (chalah - your favour)', type 102 action (not volition or affect: an outward deed). Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'the people of Tyre / the rich', target 107 'the queen (her favour)'. Crucially manner 108 is present with a value - 'with gifts' - the one place in the seek-family so far where the mode is specified: the entreaty is carried by wealth. Coupling 112 is 'none' - the act is not welded to a further interior movement. Intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false; prohibition 113 present:false. Operation 106 'seek favour'. Discovery 114: the nations courting the queen, the wealthy suing to soften the honoured bride's face. Locus 116 is external:person and role 115 characteristic: this is the one clearly outward-social reading - seeking directed not at God or at destroying a life but at winning a human being's favour, and doing so through gifts.
narratives.story: The people of Tyre, the richest of them, will seek the queen's favour with gifts. Seeking here is a social act - courting someone's goodwill, trying to soften a great person's face - and unusually the verse tells us how it is done: with presents. Its aim is not God and not harm but simply the favour of an honoured person. Nothing is joined to it inwardly and nothing is forbidden; it is the plain picture of the wealthy suing for the regard of the bride.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'seek / inquire after (darash - who seek after God)', type 102 action. Here source 103 IS present, as a pair resolved by span: 'the object of God's looking down from heaven (v2)' - the seeking is set within God's downward search, its source-frame the divine gaze. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'any of mankind', target 107 God. Manner 108 'none'. Coupling 112 is a span pair: 'paired with understanding' - seeking welded to the understanding mind. Intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false; prohibition 113 present:false. Operation 106 'seek after'. Discovery 114: the Godward searching that God looks down to find - the pursuit of God that, in the whole godless race, God's own gaze discovers in no one ('they have all fallen away', v3). Locus 116 is external:god and role 115 characteristic: within the inner life the operation is the mind's turning to God, but read here through absence - the searched-for seeking that is nowhere found.
narratives.story: God looks down from heaven to see whether anyone understands and seeks him. Seeking here is inquiry after God, twinned with understanding - the searching mind turned his way. But the verse frames it inside God's own looking, and the verdict is bleak: he finds no one; all have fallen away. So the searching heart shows up in this passage precisely by its absence. Nothing is forbidden; the point is a whole race in which the seeking God searches for cannot be found.
narratives.variation_note: Near-identical in wording to Psa 14:2 but recorded distinctly: here the source is explicitly paired to God's looking-down, and the locus is registered as external:god, foregrounding the divine gaze and the total absence of any seeker ('they have all fallen away'). The difference is one of frame - Psa 14 keeps the seeker's interior in view; Psa 53 reads the same seeking through God's failed search.

narratives.narrative: The item's descent. Sense 101 'seek / hunt (baqash - seek my life)', type 102 action. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'the ruthless enemies'. Target 107 is a span pair: 'my life (nefesh)' - the seeking aimed at the psalmist's very life. Coupling 112 is a span pair: 'the murderous intent of the ruthless men'. Operation 106 'seek / hunt'. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false; prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: 'ruthless men SEEK my life' - the deadly pursuit, the enemies' settled aim to take his life, the threat the prayer answers. Locus 116 external:person, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is seeking as lethal intent - the same reaching that elsewhere goes after God here hunts a human life.
narratives.story: Ruthless men, the psalmist says, seek his life; they do not set God before them. Seeking here is hunting - a settled, murderous aim fastened on his very life. It is their deliberate act, and it is bound up with their violence. The verse does not measure it or spell out its end; it simply names the threat, the deadly pursuit that his prayer to be saved answers.
narratives.variation_note: This is baqash bent to its darkest use: the target is a human life to be taken, coupled to murderous intent. It stands opposite the same verb's Godward readings (Psa 27:4, 40:16, 70:4) - the identical act of seeking, here lethal, there devotion. The contrast of aims is the finding.

narratives.narrative: A distinct item - shachar, 'seek early / earnestly'. Sense 101 'seek early / earnestly (shachar - earnestly I seek you)', type 102 action. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'the psalmist', target 107 'God (you are my God)'. Manner 108 is present: 'earnestly, at first light' - the mode is marked, a seeking at dawn and with the whole self. Coupling 112 is a span pair: 'the seeking expressed as thirst and fainting' - the operation welded to bodily craving (soul thirsts, flesh faints). Intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false; prohibition 113 present:false. Operation 106 'seek earnestly / at dawn'. Discovery 114: 'O God, you are my God; earnestly I SEEK you' - the whole-hearted pursuit of God at dawn, the soul's first and deepest priority. Locus 116 external:god, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is seeking at its most intense - God claimed as 'my God' and sought before all else, a craving felt through the body.
narratives.story: O God, you are my God; earnestly I seek you - my soul thirsts, my body faints for you, as in a dry land. Seeking here is the soul's first and hungriest act, done at daybreak, God claimed as one's own and wanted before anything else. The verse marks how it is done - early, with the whole self - and ties it to thirst and faintness, a longing felt in the body. It is the most intense form of seeking in the whole set: not a duty but a craving for God.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'seek (baqash - those who seek to destroy my life)', type 102 action. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'the enemies'. Target 107 span pair: 'to destroy the psalmist's life'. Coupling 112 span pair: 'the murderous seeking, set against the psalmist's seeking of God (v1)'. Operation 106 'seek / hunt'. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false; prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: the enemies' deadly pursuit - the dark mirror of his own seeking of God (v1, shachar): he seeks God, they seek his life, and their end is the pit. Locus 116 external:person, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is seeking as destructive drive, explicitly counterposed in the same psalm to the psalmist's dawn-seeking of God.
narratives.story: Those who seek to destroy his life, the psalm says, will themselves go down into the depths. Seeking here is a hunt to kill, and it is set deliberately against the psalmist's own seeking of God at the psalm's opening. He reaches for God; they reach for his ruin. The verse does not grade their intent or forbid it - it simply names the murderous pursuit and its end in the pit, the dark twin of devotion.
narratives.variation_note: Same verb and same deadly target as Psa 54:3, but this reading is explicitly coupled to the psalmist's own God-seeking earlier in the psalm (v1), so the finding is the contrast held within one poem: two seekings, one toward God, one toward a life, with opposite ends.

narratives.narrative: The item turns Godward again. Sense 101 'seek (baqash - those who seek you)', type 102 action. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'those who seek God'. Operation 106 'seek God' (event, inferred to its target-span). Target 107 God. Coupling 112 span pair: 'paired with those who hope in God' - the seekers welded to the hopers. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false; prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: 'let not those who SEEK you be brought to dishonor through me' - the God-seekers whose honour the psalmist guards, praying his own plight not spread shame among them: the solidarity of the faithful. Locus 116 external:god, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is seeking as a bond of fellowship - the seeker so joined to fellow seekers that he fears his shame could stain them.
narratives.story: The psalmist prays that those who hope in God, those who seek him, not be put to shame because of him. Seeking here binds a person to others who seek God - a fellowship of the faithful. His concern is not for himself but that his troubles not spill dishonour onto them. Nothing is measured or forbidden; the seeking is simply the shared devotion that makes their honour his care.
narratives.variation_note: Here baqash's God-seeking is corporate and protective - the psalmist shielding fellow seekers from shame. It differs from the private longing of Psa 27:4 and the joyful outward prayer of Psa 40:16 by foregrounding solidarity: seeking as the tie that makes him fear for others' honour.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'seek (darash - you who seek God)', type 102 action. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'those who seek God'. Operation 106 'seek God'. Target 107 God. Coupling 112 span pair: 'the seekers whose hearts revive' - the operation welded to the reviving of the heart. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false, the revival carried inside the coupling. Prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: 'you who SEEK God, let your hearts revive' - the God-seekers called to fresh life, their flagging hearts quickened by seeing God hear the needy. Locus 116 external:god, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is seeking whose fruit is revival - the seeking heart re-enlivened when it sees God answer the afflicted.
narratives.story: When the humble see God act they are glad, and the word goes out: you who seek God, let your hearts revive. Seeking here is answered with new life - tired hearts lifted again by watching God hear the needy. The verse ties the seeking straight to that revival. It sets no measure and forbids nothing; the seeker's reward is a heart brought back to life.
narratives.variation_note: Among the darash God-seek readings, this one's distinctive fruit is revival of the heart, sparked by seeing God rescue the needy. It differs from Psa 9:10's not-forsaking and Psa 14:2's God-searches-for-seekers by resolving into the quickening of a flagging inner life.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'seek (baqash - who seek my life)', type 102 action. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'the enemies'. Operation 106 'seek / hunt'. Target 107 span pair: 'the psalmist's life'. Coupling 112 span pair: 'paired with those who delight in his hurt'. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false; prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: 'Let them be put to shame... who SEEK my life' - the murderous hunters, over against those who seek God (v4): two kinds of seeking, one deadly, one blessed. Locus 116 external:person, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is lethal seeking, coupled to malicious delight and set in the same psalm against the blessed seeking of God.
narratives.story: Let them be shamed, the psalmist prays, who seek his life - the ones who delight in his hurt. Seeking here is a hunt to kill, joined to the enemies' pleasure in his pain, and the same psalm sets it directly against those who seek God. He asks that this deadly seeking be turned back. The verse neither grades nor permits it; it simply names the murderous pursuit and prays for its defeat.
narratives.variation_note: Paired within Psalm 70 against Psa 70:4's God-seekers, this baqash reading is the deadly one - coupled to delight in his hurt. The finding is the two seekings held in one short psalm: the same verb aimed at a life to destroy versus aimed at God, ending in shame versus joy.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'seek (baqash - all who seek you)', type 102 action. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'all who seek God'. Operation 106 'seek God'. Target 107 God. Coupling 112 span pair: 'issues in rejoicing and gladness in God'. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false, the joy held in the coupling. Prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: 'May all who SEEK you rejoice and be glad in you!' - the blessed seeking of God, whose reward is joy, over against those who seek the psalmist's life (v2): the same verb, opposite ends. Locus 116 external:god, role 115 characteristic: within the inner life this is Godward seeking that issues in gladness, the bright counterpart to the deadly seeking two verses earlier.
narratives.story: May all who seek God rejoice and be glad in him, the psalmist prays; may those who love his salvation always say, 'God is great.' Seeking here is Godward, and it ends in joy. In the very same psalm it stands opposite the enemies who seek his life: one seeking leads to gladness, the other to shame. The verse sets no measure and no ban; the blessed seeking of God simply overflows into rejoicing.
narratives.variation_note: The bright pole of Psalm 70's paired seekings: same verb as Psa 70:2 but aimed at God, resolving in joy rather than the shame prayed on the life-hunters. The identical word with opposite bearers and opposite ends is the finding.

narratives.narrative: Sense 101 'seek (baqash - who seek my hurt)', type 102 action. Source 103 present:false. Seat 104 'none'. Bearer 105 'the enemies'. Operation 106 'seek'. Target 107 span pair: 'the psalmist's hurt'. Coupling 112 span pair: 'the same seeking his hurt at the psalm's close (v24)'. Manner 108 'none'; intensity 109, specifier 110, effect 111 present:false; prohibition 113 present:false. Discovery 114: 'may those who SEEK my hurt be covered with scorn' - the enemies bent on his harm, whom he prays God will shame, answered at the close (v24) when they are disappointed. The verse does not measure or license it; it names the malice and asks God to turn it back - a request the psalm later reports as granted.

narratives.story: In the day of his trouble the psalmist seeks the Lord; through the night his hand stays stretched out and never tires. Seeking here is dogged and sleepless - a reaching for God that keeps on even while the soul refuses to be comforted. The verse marks how it is done: untiring, all night long. It is his own act under distress, and nothing is set against it; the picture is of a person who will not give up seeking God even when nothing consoles.
narratives.variation_note: This darash reading is seeking under duress and refusal of comfort - persistent, night-long reaching. It differs from the settled corporate readings (Psa 24:6) and the rewarded readings (Psa 34:10) by foregrounding effortful, unconsoled pursuit rather than fruit received.

Seeking here is real but compelled - a turning to God that only death could force out of them. It comes together with a repentance the sword extracted. The verse neither praises nor condemns the degree of it; it simply reports the uncomfortable fact that these hearts sought God only when they were being slain.
narratives.variation_note: Of the three 'sought' readings, this is the coerced one - seeking dragged out by judgment, not the fear-freeing seeking of Psa 34:4 nor the precept-seeking of Psa 119:45. The finding is that the same act can be produced by love or by the sword, and here it is the sword.

narratives.story: The same verse says they sought God earnestly - the eager, early kind of seeking. Here too, though, it comes under the rod: they searched for God keenly, but only because judgment had fallen. The verse holds the two together without smoothing it over: the seeking looks wholehearted, yet it was the blow that produced it. Nothing is measured or forbidden; the plain point is earnest seeking born of being struck.

This is inquiry gone dark - not a search for truth or for God but a shared plotting, minds working in concert to devise harm. It is a deliberate act of the conspirators. The verse sets no measure and no ban on it; it simply shows the collusion, the taking of counsel aimed at God's own.

narratives.story: The psalmist prays that his enemies' faces be filled with shame so that they might seek God's name. Seeking here is the very thing hoped for from foes - that their humbling would turn them to God. It is not something they are doing but something desired for them, drawn out of their disgrace. The verse forbids nothing and measures nothing; the remarkable point is that even enemies are wished into seeking God, their shame the door to it.
narratives.variation_note: Unusually for an enemy-borne baqash reading, the target is God's name and the aim is redemptive - seeking hoped for FROM the foes through shame, not the foes seeking a life to destroy (Psa 54:3, 70:2). The difference is the direction: their seeking here would be their turning.

Seeking here is deadly intent, and it is bound up with their disregard of God - they hunt a life precisely because God is nowhere in their view. It is their deliberate aim. The verse neither grades nor forbids it; it names the murderous pursuit of the godless, malice with no thought of God.
narratives.variation_note: Like Psa 54:3 and 70:2 this is baqash as lethal hunt, but here it is explicitly coupled to the enemies' godlessness ('they do not set you before them') and its locus is registered internally - the finding is malice that hunts a life BECAUSE God is shut out.

Seeking here is the disposition of the true worshipper - the heart set toward God - and it is joined to joy: to seek him is to have a rejoicing heart. Seeking here is resolute worship - a firm, purposeful turning to God and to his power - set right beside the call to seek his presence without ceasing. It is the worshipper's deliberate act. It is his own act, the turning of his whole self toward God through God's word. It recurs at Psa 119:2, the same whole-hearted seeking of God.

narratives.story: I shall walk in a wide place, the psalmist says, for I have sought your precepts. Seeking here is already done, and its fruit is freedom - a broad, open place to walk. It was his own reaching, aimed at God's word. The verse measures nothing and forbids nothing; the plain claim is that seeking out God's precepts is what opens life up into a wide place. It recurs later in the same psalm.
narratives.variation_note: Of the three 'sought' readings, this one aims at God's precepts and yields liberty ('a wide place'), unlike Psa 34:4 (God sought, fear dissolved) and Psa 78:34 (God sought under compulsion of judgment). The object is the word and the fruit is spaciousness of life.

Seeking here appears only by its lack - a settled failure to turn to God's word - and that very absence is why rescue stays out of their reach. It is not a single missed act but the shape of who they are. The verse measures nothing and forbids nothing; the point is stark: not seeking God is why they are far from salvation.
narratives.variation_note: Alone among the seek readings this is typed as disposition and read as negation - the wicked's standing failure to seek God's statutes, given as the cause of their distance from salvation. It is the dark pole of Psa 119:10's whole-hearted seeking within the same psalm.

narratives.story: For the sake of God's house, the psalmist resolves, I will seek your good - the good of Jerusalem. Seeking here is goodwill turned into action: love for his fellow worshippers and for God's dwelling moving him to work for the city's welfare. It is his own settled resolve. The verse measures nothing and forbids nothing; seeking here simply means committing himself to pursue another's good.
narratives.variation_note: The only baqash reading aimed at a city's welfare rather than God or a victim - seeking as benevolent resolve for Jerusalem's good, springing from love of kin and God's house. It shares the verb's active drive with the enemy readings but bends it wholly toward another's flourishing.
